raw_case_text:
A 25-year-old man from Ghana was admitted to our hospital for an altered mental state, weight loss, neck pain, cough, fever, nausea, vomiting, and photophobia for 7 days. He reported a cough with greenish phlegm and blood-tinged sputum and a weight loss of ~20 lb in the last month. He reported that he could not eat because he was always nauseous and experienced nonbilious, nonprojectile vomiting. He denied chest pain, difficulty breathing and swallowing, diarrhea, dysuria, and skin rashes. His past medical history included intermittent asthma and migraines, but he was not on any medications. He did not have any significant family history or prior surgeries. He reported that he smoked 10 cigarettes a day for the past 5 years, drank alcohol occasionally, and denied illicit drug use except for marijuana. He reported that he last traveled to Ghana 6 months priorly, and he denied having contact with sick persons. He reported that he was sexually active with many partners but denied any prior sexually transmitted diseases.
Examination revealed a cachectic young male with a heart rate of 102 beats/min, a blood pressure of 108/69 mmHg, a respiratory rate of 20 breaths/min, a temperature of 98 F, and a 96% oxygen saturation in ambient air. He had a body mass index of 19.2 kg/m2 and was lethargic but oriented. He had no icterus or cervical or axillary lymphadenopathy. He had clear bilateral breath sounds, and his cardiovascular and abdominal examinations were unremarkable. He had a good pulse and no peripheral edema.
On admission, the patient tested positive for HIV with a CD4 count less than 20 and a high viral load. Pneumonia and meningitis resulting from opportunistic infections were considered, and he was treated for bacterial meningitis and tuberculosis (TB) even though the lumbar puncture was delayed because the patient was restless and uncooperative. The lumbar puncture results showed a pressure of 23 cm H2O, a white blood cell count of 2, a red blood cell count of 57, a protein level of 102 mg/dl, and a glucose level of 25 mg/dl. The Gram stain and bacterial antigen tests were negative.
There was a high suspicion of pulmonary TB and tuberculous meningitis due to recent travel to Ghana, and the initial chest X-ray showed multiple nodular opacities suggestive of miliary TB (Figure 1(a)). The micronodular appearance was confirmed by a chest CT scan without contrast (Figure 1(b)). Despite a quantiFERON negative test result, quadruple therapy for TB with isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol, and rifampin (RIPE) was continued.
On succeeding days, yeast was growing in the patient's blood cultures and a Gram stain of the patient's cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) showed presence of yeast cells. The titer of Cryptococcus in the CSF was greater than 1 : 1024 and was eventually identified as Cryptococcus neoformans. Thus, antibacterial meningitis treatment was discontinued, and the patient was started on amphotericin B and flucytosine. Anti-TB medications were continued. He underwent placement of a lumbar drain due to a persistent headache and photophobia. Antiretroviral treatment was not started, but the patient was treated with prophylaxis medications for opportunistic infections. At this time, the patient had four persistently negative acid-fast bacilli sputum smears and was negative for the sputum Mycobacterium tuberculosis PCR test.
The patient underwent FFB with BAL and TBBx. In the BAL, >100,000 CFU/mL of Staphylococcus haemolyticus grew; thus, the treatment for bacterial pneumonia was modified. Tissue culture and TBBx showed the presence of Cryptococcus neoformans. Higher magnification microscopy showed the presence of both hyphae and yeast cells (Figures 2(a) and 2(b)). The patient showed clinical improvement and was discharged on oral fluconazole.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 25-year-old Ghanaian man presented with a 7-day history of altered mental status, neck pain, cough with greenish blood-tinged sputum, fever, nausea, vomiting, and photophobia, and a 20-pound weight loss over 1 month.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 7 days prior to admission, the patient developed altered mental status, neck pain, photophobia, fever, persistent nausea with non-bilious vomiting, and a productive cough with greenish, blood-tinged phlegm, superimposed on an unintentional 20-pound weight loss over the preceding month. He had traveled to Ghana 6 months earlier.
subjective.past_medical_history: Intermittent asthma and migraines; smoker (10 cigarettes/day for 5 years), occasional alcohol and marijuana use; sexually active with multiple partners; traveled to Ghana 6 months prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for altered mental status, ~20-lb weight loss, neck pain, productive hemoptysis/green sputum cough, fever, nausea, vomiting, and photophobia. Negative for chest pain, dyspnea, dysphagia, diarrhea, dysuria, or skin rashes. No home medications.

objective.physical_examination: Cachectic (BMI 19.2 kg/m2), lethargic but oriented; heart rate 102 beats/min, blood pressure 108/69 mmHg, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, temperature 98 F, room air SpO2 96%. No jaundice, lymphadenopathy, or peripheral edema, with clear bilateral breath sounds and unremarkable cardiovascular and abdominal exams.
objective.routine_investigations: Positive HIV test with high HIV viral load; negative QuantiFERON-TB, 4 negative sputum AFB smears, and negative sputum M. tuberculosis PCR; blood cultures grew Cryptococcus neoformans. Chest X-ray showed diffuse miliary-like nodular opacities.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count was <20 cells/uL. Non-contrast chest CT confirmed diffuse bilateral miliary micronodules. Lumbar puncture revealed opening pressure 23 cmH2O, WBC 2/uL, RBC 57/uL, elevated protein 102 mg/dL, low glucose 25 mg/dL, yeast cells on CSF Gram stain, and CSF Cryptococcus neoformans antigen titer >1:1024. Flexible fiberoptic bronchoscopy with BAL and transbronchial biopsy (TBBx) grew >100,000 CFU/mL Staphylococcus haemolyticus on BAL and demonstrated Cryptococcus neoformans (showing both yeast and pseudohyphal/hyphal forms) on TBBx histology and tissue culture.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of newly diagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS (CD4 <20 cells/uL) complicated by disseminated Cryptococcus neoformans infection (meningitis, fungemia, and miliary pulmonary cryptococcosis mimicking miliary tuberculosis) and Staphylococcus haemolyticus pneumonia, confirmed by blood, CSF, and transbronchial lung biopsy cultures, CSF CrAg titer >1:1024, and lung biopsy microscopy showing yeast and hyphal forms of C. neoformans; miliary tuberculosis was ruled out by negative QuantiFERON, 4 AFB smears, and MTB PCR. Treated with amphotericin B and flucytosine, lumbar drain placement for refractory intracranial hypertension/headache, targeted antibiotics for S. haemolyticus, and opportunistic infection prophylaxis (while deferring ART initiation during acute CM induction), discharging clinically improved on oral fluconazole.
